pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach campground on Orcas Island with boat launch and trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Obstruction Pass State Park is one of the few public beaches on Orcas Island. A half-mile trail leads through forest to the bluff and down to the pebbly beach. The park has a boat launch and nine first-come, first-served campsites.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and trail camping on Camano Island near Seattle with rocky shoreline and forest hiking.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 244-acre state park on Camano Island offers 6,700 feet of rocky shoreline and beach access. Forest loop trails provide hiking, while the shoreline is suited for birding, shell and rock exploration, with views of Puget Sound, the Olympic Mountains, and Mount Rainier.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Desert fishing park with shade trees in Yakima, Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Yakima Sportsman State Park is a 266-acre park created to promote game management and preserve natural resources. The irrigated grounds feature deciduous trees throughout the camping and picnic areas, offering shade in the surrounding desert.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 197-acre year-round park at the confluence of the Wenatchee and Columbia rivers in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Wenatchee Confluence State Park is a 197-acre year-round camping park where the Wenatchee and Columbia rivers meet. The north section offers recreation area camping, while the south section is a designated natural wetland. The park provides access to downtown Wenatchee, Rocky Reach Dam and fish ladder, and Leavenworth.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beachside camping on the Wanapum Reservoir along the Columbia River in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Wanapum Recreational Area offers camping within Ginkgo Petrified Forest State Park, a 7,470-acre park with 27,000 feet of freshwater shoreline on the Wanapum Reservoir. The park features the Ginkgo Petrified Forest, a registered national natural landmark discovered in the late 1920s.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside and riverside camping on the west side of the Cascades with a 265-foot waterfall.
pitches.description_rewrite: Wallace Falls State Park spans 1,380 acres with shoreline on the Wallace River, Wallace Lake, Jay Lake and Shaw Lake. The park features a 265-foot waterfall and old-growth coniferous forests. Swimming is available 5 miles east at Big Eddy along the Skykomish River.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on the Pacific coast near Westport with trails through shore pines and dunes.
pitches.description_rewrite: Twin Harbors State Park is a 222-acre camping area on the Pacific coast, 4 miles south of Westport. Beach trails wind through shore pines before opening to sand dunes and dune grass.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on the forested south shore of Lake Chelan in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Twenty-Five Mile Creek State Park is a 235-acre camping park on the forested south shore of Lake Chelan. The park has a modern marina and separates the mountains from the lake.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Marine camping on Hood Canal with beach access and saltwater swimming in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Twanoh State Park is a 182-acre marine camping park with 3,167 feet of saltwater shoreline on Hood Canal in South Puget Sound. The park is known for warm saltwater swimming and abundant shellfish.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping at Dry Falls with beach access, fishing, and hiking trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park is a 4,027-acre park with 73,640 feet of freshwater shoreline at the foot of Dry Falls. The 400-foot-high cliff overlooks deep gorges and reflective lakes. The park offers trout fishing, hiking trails, and golf.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Banks Lake with 50,000 feet of freshwater shoreline.
pitches.description_rewrite: Steamboat Rock State Park is a 5,043-acre park on Banks Lake with three campground areas and day-use facilities. The park features 50,000 feet of shoreline and a distinctive 600-acre columnar basaltic rock formation.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beachfront camping on Lopez Island with boating, fishing, crabbing and clamming.
pitches.description_rewrite: Spencer Spit State Park is a 200-acre marine and camping park on Lopez Island in the Strait of Juan de Fuca. The park offers excellent crabbing, clamming and car-top boating, with a sand spit enclosed by a salt-chuck lagoon. Restrooms are available; showers are located in Lopez.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and trail camping on Puget Sound's Olympic Peninsula in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Sequim Bay State Park is a 92-acre marine camping park with 4,909 feet of saltwater coastline on the Olympic Peninsula. The park hosts a section of the Olympic Discovery Trail, a 120-mile multi-use recreation trail extending from Port Townsend to the Pacific Ocean. Open year-round.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping among pines near Mount St. Helens in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 475-acre year-round park sits among pines with forested campgrounds and hiking trails. Silver Lake is adjacent to the campground, and a pedestrian tunnel connects to the Mount St. Helens Interpretive Center and a boardwalk trail over wetlands.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Satsop River with fishing for steelhead, cutthroat trout and salmon.
pitches.description_rewrite: Schafer State Park is a 119-acre campground on the Satsop River, midway between Olympia and the Pacific Ocean. Fish for steelhead, cutthroat trout and salmon, or wade in calm, shallow spots and tube down the river.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Hood Canal with 1,500 feet of saltwater beachfront.
pitches.description_rewrite: Scenic Beach State Park is a 121-acre camping park on Hood Canal with 1,500 feet of saltwater beachfront. The park features a restored 1923 Emel House and gazebo, and is known for wild native rhododendrons in spring.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Puget Sound between Tacoma and Seattle.
pitches.description_rewrite: Saltwater State Park is a 137-acre park with 1,445 feet of saltwater shoreline on Puget Sound, located halfway between Tacoma and Seattle. The park was dedicated in 1926 when the two cities buried a hatchet as a symbol of ending their rivalry. The park sits on the flight path of Sea-Tac International Airport.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Horse-friendly campground on 12,000 acres along the Spokane River north of Spokane.
pitches.description_rewrite: Riverside State Park spans 12,000 acres along the Spokane and Little Spokane rivers with nearly 200,000 feet of shoreline. The park features Ponderosa pines, lakes, marshes and wildlife. Equestrian campers can access 25 miles of trails and an obstacle course with a 60-foot round pen.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Skagit River in Washington with eagle watching.
pitches.description_rewrite: Rasar State Park is a 169-acre campground with 4,000 feet of shoreline on the Skagit River. Wildlife observation, especially eagle watching, can be excellent in early fall and winter.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside campground on the Chehalis River in Washington with hiking trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Rainbow Falls State Park is a 139-acre camping area with 3,400 feet of shoreline on the Chehalis River. Miles of loamy trails wind through the forest and along the river, leading to a small cascade.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beachfront camping on Hood Canal with boat launch access in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Potlatch State Park is a 125-acre camping area with 5,700 feet of saltwater shoreline on Hood Canal. The park offers boat launch access and is popular for shellfish harvesting, diving, and kayaking.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Freshwater beach and fishing on O'Sullivan Reservoir in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Potholes State Park is a 775-acre park with 6,000 feet of shoreline on O'Sullivan Reservoir. The park welcomes boaters, fishers, and swimmers in a desert setting with freshwater marshes.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Forested marine park on Puget Sound with beach and trails in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Penrose Point State Park is a 165-acre park on the shores of Puget Sound with nearly 2 miles of saltwater frontage on Mayo Cove and Carr Inlet. Trails wind through Douglas-fir, western red cedar, red alder, Pacific madrone and big-leaf maple, with ferns, huckleberry and trillium in the understory.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping in north central Washington with hiking trails and waterfront access.
pitches.description_rewrite: Pearrygin Lake State Park is a 1,185-acre park near Winthrop with 11,000 feet of waterfront on Pearrygin Lake and 6.5 miles of hiking trails. Winter recreation, including fat-tire snow bicycling, is available after November 1.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Lewis River in Washington, 15 miles north of Vancouver.
pitches.description_rewrite: Paradise Point State Park is an 88-acre camping park with 6,180 feet of freshwater shoreline on the Lewis River, located 15 miles north of Vancouver. The park offers unguarded swimming and campsites in open grass or wooded areas, plus a small apple orchard.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on 2,300 feet of ocean shoreline north of Aberdeen.
pitches.description_rewrite: Pacific Beach State Park is a 10-acre camping park with 2,300 feet of ocean shoreline north of Aberdeen. Walk, picnic, or fly a kite on the flat sandy beach. Small beach fires are allowed more than 100 feet from vegetation.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 170-acre beach camping park in Washington with ocean, dunes and shore pine forest.
pitches.description_rewrite: Ocean City State Park is a 170-acre year-round camping park with ocean beach, dunes, and shore pine thickets. The park backs North Bay Natural Preserve, a shallow bay with wetland streams and mudflats. Ocean Shores nearby offers shopping, dining, and an 18-hole golf course.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Mountaintop camping in the Selkirk Mountains near Spokane, Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Mount Spokane State Park is a 12,444-acre park in the Selkirk Mountains with 100 miles of trails and views from 5,883-foot Mount Spokane. Summer camping includes one campsite and a lookout. The park receives 300 inches of snow in winter.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 5,252-acre park in Washington with lakes, hiking, and equestrian trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Moran State Park offers 130 campsites plus a group camp across 5,252 acres. Enjoy swimming and non-motorized boating on five freshwater lakes, plus 38 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. Mount Constitution provides expansive views of the San Juan archipelago, with a historic stone tower at the summit.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Deep Lake with beaches, trails, and water activities in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Millersylvania State Park spans 842 acres along Deep Lake's 3,300 feet of freshwater shoreline. The park features two swimming beaches, hiking and biking trails, boat launches, and rentals for kayaks, paddleboards, and pedal boats. Fishing is available throughout the park.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Columbia River in the eastern gorge with beach and fishing.
pitches.description_rewrite: Maryhill State Park is an 89-acre camping park with 4,700 feet of waterfront on the Columbia River. The park offers camping, boating, windsurfing, fishing, a swim beach, and picnic facilities.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping near Port Orchard with saltwater shoreline, trails, and water activities.
pitches.description_rewrite: Manchester State Park is a 111-acre beach park near Port Orchard with 3,400 feet of saltwater shoreline and views of Bainbridge Island. The park features 2 miles of hiking trails, a boat launch, and opportunities for swimming, kayaking, and diving.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Lake Entiat with accessible paved trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lincoln Rock State Park is an 86-acre campground on the east side of Lake Entiat. The park features the Rocky Reach Trail, a paved ADA-accessible trail that connects to the Apple Capital Loop Trail, offering 20 miles of walking and biking paths.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Touchet River in SE Washington with trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lewis and Clark Trail State Park is a 37-acre campground with 1,333 feet of freshwater shoreline on the Touchet River. The park features ponderosa pine, alder, maple and cottonwood trees, with opportunities for birdwatching.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Old-growth forest camping with hiking and horseback riding in SW Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lewis and Clark State Park is a 616-acre camping area in old-growth forest east of I-5 and south of Chehalis. The park offers hiking and horseback riding through rare old-growth trees on the historic north spur of the Oregon Trail, with fire circles, an amphitheater, and horseshoe pits.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and lake camping on Samish Bay with fishing, hiking, and trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Larrabee State Park spans 2,748 acres with 8,100 feet of saltwater shoreline on Samish Bay. Freshwater Fragrance and Lost lakes offer bass and trout fishing, while hiking and mountain bike trails wind through Douglas-fir and salal forest. Trains pass up to 16 times daily on the adjacent Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad and Amtrak track.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside and riverside camping on glacier-fed Lake Wenatchee in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lake Wenatchee State Park offers 489 acres of camping with 12,623 feet of waterfront on Lake Wenatchee and the Wenatchee River. The lake is popular for boating and windsurfing, with boat rentals and kayak and standup paddleboard rentals available near the shore.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Wooded lakeside campground in Washington with swimming and fishing.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lake Sylvia State Park is a 252-acre camping area with 15,000 feet of freshwater shoreline. The park offers swimming and fishing on its lake, and accommodates day and group camping trips.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Forested lakeside park on Lake Easton with boat launch, fishing, swimming, and trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lake Easton State Park is a 516-acre forested camping area on the shores of Lake Easton with 24,000 feet of freshwater access. The park offers boat launch, fishing, swimming, and trail access including the Palouse to Cascade State Park Trail. Winter activities include cross-country skiing and snowmobiling on groomed trails.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Lake Chelan's forested south shore in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Lake Chelan State Park is a 127-acre camping park on the forested south shore of Lake Chelan, with 6,000 feet of shoreline and beach access by stairs. The park offers hiking trails and serves as a base for exploring the North Cascades.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach campground with saltwater shoreline and fishing in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Kitsap Memorial State Park spans 58 acres with 1,797 feet of saltwater shoreline. The park offers fishing, two playing fields for Frisbee and other games, and a log hall available for weddings.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Green River with boat launch access in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 320-acre state park sits on a forested plateau with 2 miles of Green River shoreline. Hand-launch boat and raft access is available. Expert-level river rafting and kayaking trips run through the Green River Gorge.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Puget Sound with boat launch, fishing, and trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Joemma Beach State Park is a 106-acre marine camping park with 3,000 feet of saltwater frontage on Puget Sound's Key Peninsula. The park has the only boat launch with vehicle parking on Key Peninsula, plus a pier, dock, and mooring buoys. Trails and tidepooling are available.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and swimming campground on Harstine Island in Puget Sound.
pitches.description_rewrite: Jarrell Cove State Park is a 67-acre marine camping park with 3,500 feet of saltwater shoreline on Harstine Island. The park offers swimming, diving, and boating opportunities, plus an amphitheater and sports fields.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Marine camping on Port Orchard Bay with saltwater beach access in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Illahee State Park is a 75-acre marine park with 1,785 feet of saltwater frontage on Port Orchard Bay. The park features old-growth timber, including one of the nation's largest yew trees, and a veterans' war memorial.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Mayfield Lake with boating, fishing, swimming and trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 421-acre park sits on the north shore of Mayfield Lake with 46,000 feet of freshwater shoreline. Enjoy boating, fishing, swimming, hiking trails, birding, wildlife viewing and horseshoe pits.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on 412 acres with ocean frontage near Grayland, WA.
pitches.description_rewrite: Year-round marine camping park with 7,449 feet of ocean frontage. Offers 55 full-hookup campsites, 16 yurts, 4 standard sites, and 4 primitive tent sites within walking distance of the beach.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 433-acre state park with 2+ miles of saltwater beach on Washington's coast.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fort Worden Historical State Park spans 433 acres with over 2 miles of saltwater shoreline. The park features a full-service conference center available for day and multi-day events. Built between 1898 and 1917, Fort Worden was part of the coastal defense system called the Triangle of Fire.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 414-acre marine park with saltwater beach on Port Townsend Bay in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fort Townsend State Park offers 3,960 feet of saltwater shoreline on Port Townsend Bay across 414 forested acres. The park preserves military history with interpretive plaques along Officers' Row and a historic World War II torpedo tower now part of the group campground.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on 1,454 acres of saltwater shoreline in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fort Flagler Historical State Park spans 1,454 acres surrounded by 19,100 feet of saltwater shoreline on three sides. Part of the historic "Triangle of Fire" forts, it offers insight into military and maritime history.

pitches.elevator_pitch: 649-acre park on Whidbey Island with 25 miles of mixed-use trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fort Ebey State Park offers 25 miles of mixed-use walking and bike trails, plus 3 miles of bike-only trails. The bluff trail overlooks Admiralty Inlet with views of Point Wilson Lighthouse, while forested trails wind through Douglas-fir and hemlock with pink big-leaf rhododendrons in season.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Marine camping on Puget Sound with 10,810 feet of saltwater shoreline.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fort Casey Historical State Park is a 998-acre marine camping park on Puget Sound's Admiralty Inlet, featuring 10,810 feet of saltwater shoreline and Keystone Spit, a 2-mile stretch of land separating Admiralty Inlet and Crocket Lake.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Forested camping in the Blue Mountains of southeastern Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Fields Spring State Park is an 825-acre forested park in the Blue Mountains of southeastern Washington. Trails wind through Puffer Butte and surrounding hills that bloom with wildflowers in spring, display russet and sapphire tones in summer, and offer snow activities in winter.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and riverside camping on Hood Canal with forest and delta access.
pitches.description_rewrite: Dosewallips State Park offers 1,039 acres of year-round camping with 5 miles of Hood Canal shoreline and the Dosewallips River. The park features riverside campsites, cabins, and platform tents set in a moss-carpeted forest with a shell-strewn delta.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Marine and camping park on two islands with saltwater and freshwater shoreline.
pitches.description_rewrite: Deception Pass State Park spans 4,134 acres across Fidalgo and Whidbey islands, connected by two bridges. The park features 77,000 feet of saltwater shoreline and 33,900 feet of freshwater shoreline on three lakes.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Puget Sound in Western Washington with saltwater shoreline.
pitches.description_rewrite: Dash Point State Park sits on the Puget Sound near Seattle, Tacoma, and Federal Way. The 398-acre park offers 3,301 feet of saltwater beach with views of the sound and opportunities for sea-life study.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Riverside camping on the Columbia River in Washington's desert scablands.
pitches.description_rewrite: Daroga State Park is a 90-acre camping park with 1.5 miles of Columbia River shoreline on the elevated edge of the desert scablands. Desert Canyon Golf Course is located 2 miles away.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside and riverside camping 8 miles from Republic in north-central Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Curlew Lake State Park is an 87-acre camping park 8 miles from Republic. Water sports are available in summer and snow sports in winter. Ranald MacDonald's Grave, a State Parks heritage site, is nearby along a 25-mile scenic drive by the Kettle River near the Canadian Border.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on freshwater reservoirs in north central Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Conconully State Park is an 81-acre camping park with 5,400 feet of freshwater shoreline. Fish for smallmouth bass, rainbow trout, and kokanee in the lower Conconully Reservoir or Upper Conconully Lake, or enjoy waterskiing.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside and riverside camping on the Columbia River in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Columbia Hills State Park is a 3,638-acre park on the Columbia River with tent and RV campsites at Horsethief Lake. The park offers watercraft launches and seasonal kayak rentals, plus Native American pictographs and petroglyphs at the Temani Pesh-Wa exhibit.
pitches.best_for: tent camping, RV camping, boating, equestrian

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach and riverside camping on the Long Beach Peninsula in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Cape Disappointment State Park is a 1,882-acre camping park on the Long Beach Peninsula, fronted by the Pacific Ocean and at the mouth of the Columbia River. The park offers yurts, cabins, and historic vacation homes.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Remote seasonal campground in the Simcoe Mountains near Goldendale, Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Brooks Memorial State Park is a 700-acre seasonal campground in the Simcoe Mountains, 15 miles north of Goldendale off Highway 97. Goldendale Observatory State Park is 20 minutes away for night sky viewing.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping on Rufus Woods Lake in a 748-acre desert park.
pitches.description_rewrite: Bridgeport State Park offers 748 acres of camping with 7,500 feet of freshwater shoreline on Rufus Woods Lake, located directly behind Chief Joseph Dam. The park features 18 acres of lawn and shade in desert terrain.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Forested riverside campground on the Bogachiel River on Washington's Olympic Peninsula.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 123-acre state park sits on the banks of the Bogachiel River in a thickly forested setting. It serves as a base for exploring the Olympic Peninsula, including the nearby Hoh Rainforest and Hoh River.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Boat-in marine camping on a 476-acre island with beaches, trails, and fishing.
pitches.description_rewrite: Blake Island Marine State Park is a 476-acre marine camping park reachable only by boat. The island features 5 miles of saltwater beach, miles of trails through forested interior, fishing, clamming in season, and scuba diving. Cascadia Marine Trail campsites are available at the west end.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Birch Bay's saltwater shoreline in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Birch Bay State Park is a 194-acre camping park with 8,255 feet of saltwater shoreline on Birch Bay and 14,923 feet of freshwater shoreline on Terrell Creek. The park protects the Terrell Creek Marsh, one of the few remaining saltwater/freshwater estuaries in north Puget Sound, and includes a natural game sanctuary at its north end.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach camping on Hood Canal's saltwater shoreline in western Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Belfair State Park is a 65-acre year-round campground on 3,720 feet of saltwater shoreline at the southern end of Hood Canal. The park offers summer interpretive programs, grass fields, warm waters, and a playground.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Year-round camping in the Columbia River Gorge with hiking, biking, and equestrian trails.
pitches.description_rewrite: Beacon Rock State Park is a 4,456-acre camping park in the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area. The park features 9,500 feet of Columbia River shoreline and over 20 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian use.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Beach campground on Padilla Bay with saltwater shoreline in Washington.
pitches.description_rewrite: Bay View State Park offers 25 acres of camping on 1,285 feet of saltwater shoreline on Padilla Bay. The Breazeale Padilla Bay Interpretive Center, a half-mile away, features exhibits and hands-on activities focused on the estuary.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside horse camp in Washington with trails, swimming, and fishing.
pitches.description_rewrite: This 280-acre park features a spring-fed lake for swimming and paddling, stocked with trout for fishing. Hiking and biking trails plus primitive equestrian camping and horse trails.

pitches.elevator_pitch: Lakeside camping in Washington's pine forests with trout fishing and water sports.
pitches.description_rewrite: Alta Lake State Park spans 174 acres where pine forests meet the desert. The 2-mile-long lake offers trout fishing, waterskiing, and windsurfing. Lake Chelan is 30 minutes away.
